questions.question: You have a green light, but traffic is blocking the intersection ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Wait until traffic clears before entering the intersection.
Follow other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until traffic clears before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter the intersection if other vehicles are blocking your way. If you enter and the light turns red, your vehicle will block cross traffic. You can get a ticket for blocking an intersection.

questions.question: Where should you place your hands when using hand-to-hand steering?

options.text: Left hand at 9-10 o'clock and right hand at 2-3 o'clock
Left hand at 10-11 o'clock and right hand at 1-2 o'clock
Left hand at 7-8 o'clock and right hand at 4-5 o'clock

questions.correctAnswerText: Left hand at 7-8 o'clock and right hand at 4-5 o'clock
questions.explanation: Use hand-to-hand steering (also called push-pull steering) when driving normally above 15 mph. Think of the steering wheel as a clock. Place your left hand between 7 and 8 o'clock and your right hand between 4 and 5 o'clock.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Drive only in the direction of the arrow.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It tells drivers they must follow the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must help keep roads safe. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: When can you legally turn left at a red light after stopping?

options.text: When turning from a two-way street onto another two-way street.
When turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
When you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you may turn left at a red light only if you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street. Make sure no signs prohibit this turn.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beam headlights in fog or mist?

options.text: The light reflects back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles might not see you.
Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light reflects back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam headlights reflect light back toward you, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, you find a gap in traffic, adjust your speed to match traffic, and signal. What is your next step?

options.text: Expect traffic to give you the right-of-way and proceed.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to clear before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: After finding a gap, matching traffic speed, and signaling, merge safely into the gap. Stay alert to other traffic. Do not expect other drivers to make room for you.

questions.question: At an intersection where your view to the side is blocked, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Maintain your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.
questions.explanation: When approaching an intersection with a blocked view, slow down and stop. Then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions before proceeding.

questions.question: How can you avoid glare from oncoming headlights?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Keep your eyes on the road centerline.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights. Instead, glance toward the right side of the road. Then continue looking ahead to see where the other vehicle is.

questions.question: Your vehicle's rear is skidding to the left. What should you do?

options.text: Do not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left.
Turn your steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If you skid on wet or icy roads, take your foot off the accelerator and brakes, and turn your steering wheel in the direction the rear is skidding. However, if you have anti-lock brakes, apply the brakes firmly and steer straight ahead.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid out of control, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes lightly.
Stay off the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, do not use the brakes. Keep steering until your car is under control and moving safely again.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about traffic laws they must follow. These signs control traffic direction, lane use, turning, speed, and parking. They are usually white rectangles with black, red, or green letters or symbols.

questions.question: If your car is skidding, what should you do?

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes during a skid. Braking will make the skid worse.

questions.question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?

options.text: Stop completely, let traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
Slow down and go with caution.
Stop completely and stay stopped until the light stops flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When parallel parking while facing downhill, how should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the curb or road edge.
Turn them away from the curb or road edge.
Keep them straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply toward the curb or road edge.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb. When parking uphill without a curb, turn toward the road edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn away from the curb.

questions.question: If another car is passing you in a no-passing zone, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down to help the other car return to your lane safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to help the other car return to your lane safely.
questions.explanation: Help the passing vehicle get back into your lane as quickly as possible. This helps everyone avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: If you get a sudden flat tire while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Use the brakes lightly.
Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by easing off the gas and using light braking.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop and check traffic from both directions before going.
Let traffic on the road you want to enter have the right-of-way.
Keep a steady speed and check for traffic from all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let traffic on the road you want to enter have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A three-sided yield sign means you must slow down and be ready to stop. Let any vehicle, bike, or pedestrian pass first. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: Why should you increase your distance when driving behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see around the sides of the vehicle better.
Because drivers tend to pass large vehicles.
Because the vehicle's slipstream will pull you in.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see around the sides of the vehicle better.
questions.explanation: The driver of a large truck, bus, or van may not see you directly behind them. Increase your distance to see around the vehicle and see the road ahead.

questions.question: On a road with a single broken white centerline, what can you do?

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You can cross the centerline to change lanes.
You can only change lanes from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can cross the centerline to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines mean lanes go the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass another car when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a crosswalk where people cross the road. When you see this sign, slow down and let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, how can you avoid traffic merging from on-ramps on your right?

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Maintain your speed and position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: Watch for on-ramps on interstate highways. When you can, move to the left lane. This gives vehicles room to safely enter from the on-ramp on your right.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not permitted.
Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means you can pass another vehicle on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
School crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to situations ahead. This sign warns you that pedestrians may be crossing the road.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice, what should drivers with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal hard and keep holding it on snow or ice. The ABS will pump the brakes faster than you can.
